paragraphs: Akavya ben Mahalalel, Mishnah Bekhorot 3:4(25a); Nega'im 1:4, 5:3; Niddah 2:6. In Hillel's time, Berakhot 19a; Pesaḥim 64b. R. Yehudah bar Ilai testified the courtyard never closed on Passover eve upon an Israelite his equal in humility and fear of sin. Avot 3:1 teaches humility: consider three things, whence you came, etc. Eduyot 5:6: offered the court headship if he retracted his laws, he preferred lifelong foolishness to a moment's wickedness, lest people say he retracted for power. He told his learned son to follow the sages’ view and explained why he himself had stood by his own view on three rulings [four in Eduyot 5:7]: he had heard many sages, but his son heard only him. His son asked him to commend him to the sages. He refused: 'Your deeds will bring you close; your deeds will distance you.' After Shemayah and Avtalyon's deaths, he said a female convert is not given the sotah water. Told they had administered it, he said they gave it to her because she was a convert like them; alternatively, they gave imitation water, not basin water, to frighten her. Some say he was excommunicated; R. Yehudah bar Ilai says Heaven forbid. Yuḥasin, Seder HaDorot after the priests, suggests excommunication but not death under the ban, as Sifrei somewhat implies. Burial outside Kefar Manda, with R. Yissakhar and Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel, גא״י [provisionally Gelilot Eretz Yisrael].
